subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should plugins receive a host-managed agent-scoped key-value store, or must durable plugin state remain in the existing session-extension and plugin-owned SQLite boundaries?
rationale: The choice changes a public Plugin SDK contract and determines who controls agent identity, authorization, isolation, retention, quotas, migrations, and sensitive state.

options.title: Require Concrete Inventory First
options.body: Ask for affected plugins and state lifecycles, then use or narrowly extend the existing scoped APIs instead of adding a generic cache immediately.

options.title: Design Agent-Scoped Storage
options.body: Approve a new host-managed API only after defining namespace, authorization, quota, TTL cleanup, migration, backup, and uninstall semantics.

options.title: Extend Plugin-Owned KV
options.body: Add narrowly scoped TTL and agent-namespace support to plugin-state-runtime while keeping database ownership with each plugin.

recommendation.title: Require Concrete Inventory First
recommendation.body: Ask for affected plugins and state lifecycles, then use or narrowly extend the existing scoped APIs instead of adding a generic cache immediately.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from recent adjacent agent-runtime and Plugin SDK history.
